title: In Conversation: Founder James on How Languages Rewire the Brain
dek: Neuroplasticity, code-switching, and the timelines we draw to explain tense. Founder James (JY DM) walks through the cognitive science behind this month’s issue — and separates what the evidence supports from what the internet repeats.

blocks.text: November is the magazine’s most academic issue, and the theme is cognitive immersion: what actually happens in the brain when a second language takes up residence. The volume includes a long piece on code-switching and L2 integration, a piece on creative writing as a learning tool, a master timeline for verb tenses across five languages, and an essay on reclaiming a playful brain through neuroplasticity. It is a lot of theory, so we asked the founder to translate it.
blocks.say: November is the magazine’s most academic issue, and the theme is cognitive immersion: what actually happens in the brain when a second language takes up residence.

blocks.text: This Month: November Academia

Vol. 2026.11 is deliberately heavier than the autumn issues. Four pieces carry the theme: the COSYtalks essay on moving beyond translation into genuine L2 integration; a companion essay on creative writing, from micro-sparks to full stories; the Grammar desk’s master timeline, which sets English, French, Italian, Russian and Greek tense systems side by side; and a closing essay on neuroplasticity and the playful brain.
The through-line is a claim worth testing: that a language is not stored as a set of rules, but as a network of habits that can be rewired at any age.
